explanation: XOR every array entry, then XOR every integer in the promised range 1..n. Each required occurrence cancels its matching range occurrence, leaving the extra value.
correctness: Associativity and commutativity let matching values cancel because x XOR x=0. The input is exactly the range multiset plus one extra occurrence, so cancellation leaves that occurrence. No large sum or multiplication is formed.
walkthrough: For [3,1,4,2,3], XOR the input values, then XOR 1,2,3,4 because n=4. One copy of every required value cancels its range partner; the extra 3 remains, so return 3. The algorithm uses XOR rather than a sum formula.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1. The promise includes every value 1..n and exactly one extra occurrence; the more general pigeonhole problem has a different contract.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: process the n+1 input entries; the range sum is constant-time arithmetic, or an additional n XOR operations in the XOR variants.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: scalar accumulator and range/loop variables, with no input mutation.
